Evidence: Former Chinese CDC head Zeng Guang stated that while the coronavirus was first detected in Wuhan, it did not originate there, suggesting that the pathogen may have been circulating elsewhere prior to its detection in China (Source 1). This aligns with findings from Italian researchers indicating the virus was present in Italy months before it was identified in Wuhan. The WHO is investigating the origins of the virus, and its director-general has called for further studies, keeping all hypotheses open (Source 2).
Justification: The retrieved evidence supports the claim that it cannot be definitively stated that China is the origin of the coronavirus. Zeng Guang's assertion that the virus was first detected in Wuhan but did not originate there, along with the WHO's call for further investigation into all hypotheses, directly corroborates the claim's core assertion.
